topic: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) for Exception Safety
explanation: RAII is a C++ programming idiom that ensures resource management (such as memory, file handles, or network connections) is tied to object lifetime. By acquiring resources in constructors and releasing them in destructors, RAII guarantees that resources are properly released when objects go out of scope, even if exceptions occur. This pattern is fundamental for writing exception-safe code, preventing resource leaks, and simplifying cleanup logic in modern C++.
